source.title: HVI: A New Color Space for Low-light Image Enhancement
source.authors: Yan, Feng, Zhang, Pang, Shi, Wu, Dong, Sun, Zhang

location: quantitative table, column 'Sony-Total-Dark', row 'CIDNet (Ours)': PSNR 22.904, SSIM 0.676; dataset paragraph in the experimental settings
dataset_description_verbatim: Sony-Total-Dark. This dataset is a customized version of a SID subset [7]. To make this dataset more challenging, we convert the raw format images to sRGB images with no gamma correction, resulting in images with extreme darkness.
why_it_matters: Our claim that the Sony extreme-dark set is distributed in at least two renditions with different pixel conventions rests on this: 22.904 is reported on the authors' own sRGB conversion made with no gamma correction, not on the gamma-corrected rendition we evaluate.

correction.previous_text: Sony-Total-Dark. This dataset is a conversion of a SID subset. To make this dataset more challenging we convert the raw format images to sRGB with gamma correction, resulting in images with low brightness.
correction.what_was_wrong: The quote was reconstructed from two-column text truncated by the reading command, so 'with no gamma correction' became 'with gamma correction' and 'extreme darkness' became 'low brightness'. The field was nevertheless labelled verbatim and verified.
correction.how_verified_now: pdftotext -raw on the stored PDF, whitespace-normalised, full sentence read without truncation
correction.effect_on_the_claim: None against it: the true text names a stronger difference (no gamma curve at all), so the two-rendition claim and the 5.29 dB cross-rendition score stand.
